main_text.p: admittendum censeo , nisi quando res est desperata, quando nullum aliud victoriae po-tiundæ supereft remedium. Ut præstet eam facere ancipitem in vitâ & morte unius, quàm desperatam in congressu , & exitio totius exercitus. Ve-rum, inquit Martyr alibi, de-sperandum non est, adhibenda media, & directio Deo committenda. Verùm regero, me-dia licita adhibentur, per quæ judicamus nos commodius & melius adepturos finem desi-deratum. Et quia in aliis re-mediis nullum est præsidium, in hoc verò adhuc aliqua spes, ideo potius aliis neglectis, hoc, ut tutissimum adhibebimus. Præterquam quod si nulla spes supereffet victoriæ, aut vix ul-[?]la, si cum exercitu dimican-dum foret, quæ tamen supereft, si duorum congressus instituatur, & tamen quis velit adver-

page.notes: The word "vix ul-la" at the line end is partly obscured; the letters after "u" are unclear, so it is marked [?]. The "cum exercitu" line has a small ink blot between "cum" and "exercitu", which is not a printed letter. Long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as plain s, as the rules require (for example "censeo", "desperata", "supereft"). The catchword "fis" is printed at the lower right and continues the word "adversis" on the next page. The page shows no marginal notes, headings or italics.
